description: UrbanPy is a Python library for downloading, processing and visualising high-resolution urban data and computing accessibility metrics. It downloads city limits and points of interest from the Nominatim and Overpass APIs and population data from the Humanitarian Data Exchange, partitions a city into a hexagonal grid or administrative units, computes origin-destination and distance matrices by any mode through a routing API or a local OSRM server, finds travel times to the closest facilities, and exports the results as tables and shapefiles with Plotly maps. It is published by the Inter-American Development Bank under the EL-BID GitHub organisation. Coverage: any city that has OpenStreetMap and HDX population data. Access: source on GitHub and a pip package. Licence and cost: GNU GPL version 3, free; some routing back ends need the user's own API keys. Caveats: the README lists atomic functions as an unfinished goal, quality follows the OpenStreetMap coverage of the city, and the OSRM route needs Docker. It prepares inputs for accessibility, service coverage and facility location studies, including access to hospitals or shelters when a network link is disrupted, and builds on OpenStreetMap data and tools such as OSMnx catalogued here.
